content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Fort Collins

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: CAPM requires a secondary degree and completion of project management education—but no prior work experience. If you hold a high school diploma, associate degree, or equivalent, you're already eligible to pursue certification, making CAPM ideal for career changers and early-stage professionals in Fort Collins's growing technology, energy, and manufacturing sectors.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Hours of Instruction
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot camp. This intensive format compresses the required contact hours into a focused, interactive experience. You'll learn PMBOK® fundamentals, practice real scenarios, and interact with active certified practitioners—all from your Fort Collins location, on a schedule that fits your work commitments.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your education, submit your formal application to PMI and pay the associated exam fee. Granite PM Academy guides you through the online submission process to ensure your credentials are verified and your eligibility confirmed before you sit for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Granite PM Academy provides targeted exam-preparation resources to reinforce key concepts and build confidence. You'll take the computer-based CAPM exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. Our instructors remain available to clarify content and answer questions right up to exam day.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: CAPM certification is valid for three years. During this cycle, earn professional development units (PDUs) by attending training, conferences, or volunteering on project work. Renew by submitting your PDU record to PMI before expiration, keeping your credential current and competitive in Fort Collins's job market.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: Is the CAPM a good starting credential for {city} professionals?
fq_items.answer: Yes. The CAPM is one of the most recognized entry-level PM credentials and is highly regarded across industries in {city_state}. It demonstrates PM knowledge to employers even before you have years of experience.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.

fq_items.question: Is this training delivered online?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Our CAPM training is fully live-virtual — no travel required. {city} students attend via video conference from wherever they are.

fq_items.question: Is CAPM certification worth it for Fort Collins project managers?
fq_items.answer: Yes—CAPM is increasingly valued by Fort Collins employers in engineering, manufacturing, and healthcare, where structured project delivery is essential. Certified candidates often gain an edge in job postings and advancement, particularly at major regional employers. While not universally required, the credential signals disciplined methodology and positions you competitively in a market where PMP and CAPM credentials are cited as differentiators.

fq_items.question: Which Fort Collins employers actively hire certified project managers?
fq_items.answer: Fort Collins's largest employers—including Colorado State University, Woodward, UCHealth Poudre Valley Hospital, Advanced Energy Industries, Broadcom, and others in aerospace, clean energy, and manufacturing—increasingly seek CAPM and PMP-certified professionals. Certification is particularly valued in technology, electronics, renewable energy, and healthcare administration roles, where project governance and risk management are core competencies.
